config.title: Form Validation with Zod + React Hook Form

intro.title: Form Validation with Zod + React Hook Form
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user registration form that validates input like email and password. You will learn how to use Zod, a TypeScript-first schema library, to define validation rules. Then, you'll integrate Zod with React Hook Form to manage form state and display validation errors. This approach ensures your form data is type-safe and user-friendly.
intro.usecase: Form validation with Zod and React Hook Form is essential for building robust user interfaces in real-world Angular applications. This pattern appears in registration forms, checkout processes, and data entry dashboards where user input must be validated before submission. For example, e-commerce sites use it to validate shipping addresses and payment information, while admin panels rely on it for creating and editing database records. Developers implement this combination to ensure data integrity, provide immediate user feedback, and reduce server-side validation errors in production applications.

objectives: Construct a form using Angular's Reactive Forms module
Integrate Zod schemas with Angular form controls for validation
Configure form validation rules using Zod's validation methods
Bind form inputs to reactive form controls with proper data types
Manipulate form state and validation messages based on Zod validation results
Initialize a form with default values that comply with Zod schema requirements
Render validation feedback in the UI by connecting Zod errors to form controls

steps.title: Import Angular modules and dependencies (ReactiveFormsModule, FormBuilder, Validators, Component)
steps.instruction: Import ReactiveFormsModule, FormBuilder, and Validators from '@angular/forms', and Component from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbols you need from their respective packages.
steps.seedCode: // Import ReactiveFormsModule, FormBuilder, Validators from '@angular/forms' and Component from '@angular/core'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular modules and dependencies are imported for reactive forms and component creation.
successCriteria: ReactiveFormsModule, FormBuilder, Validators are imported from '@angular/forms', and Component is imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some of the required symbols. Make sure to import ReactiveFormsModule, FormBuilder, Validators from '@angular/forms' and Component from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import ReactiveFormsModule, FormBuilder, Validators from '@angular/forms' and Component from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the main component class with FormBuilder injection
steps.instruction: Create a component class named 'FormValidationComponent' and inject FormBuilder in its constructor.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define the component and add a constructor parameter for FormBuilder.
steps.expectedOutcome: A component class named FormValidationComponent is created with FormBuilder injected in its constructor.
successCriteria: The component class is defined with the @Component decorator and has a constructor that injects FormBuilder.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component class has the correct name and FormBuilder is properly injected in the constructor.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class wasn't created correctly. Check that you used the @Component decorator and injected FormBuilder in the constructor.

steps.title: Initialize the form group with FormBuilder
steps.instruction: Inside the FormValidationComponent class, initialize a property called 'form' using the FormBuilder's group() method. Pass an empty object as the initial controls configuration.
steps.hint: Use the injected FormBuilder instance (likely named 'fb') to call group() and assign the result to a class property.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a form group
form = this.fb.group({});
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'form' property is created in the component class, initialized with an empty FormGroup.
successCriteria: Property is a class member (not inside constructor)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're creating a property called 'form' and using the FormBuilder's group() method with an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form group initialization is missing or incorrect. Check that you're using the injected FormBuilder to create the form property.

steps.title: Set up the component template with form container
steps.instruction: Add a form element to the component's template with the formGroup binding and (ngSubmit) event handler.
steps.hint: Use the <form> element with [formGroup] bound to your form group property and (ngSubmit) bound to your onSubmit method.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Basic form structure in Angular template
<form [formGroup]="myForm" (ngSubmit)="handleSubmit()">
  <!-- Form controls go here -->
</form>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will have a form element ready to contain form controls and handle submissions.
successCriteria: The template contains a <form> element with [formGroup] binding and (ngSubmit) event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a form element, but it's missing either the formGroup binding or ngSubmit event.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form element is not properly set up with Angular bindings.

steps.title: Add name input field with form control binding
steps.instruction: In the component template, add an input field for the 'name' form control with formControlName binding.
steps.hint: Use the <input> element with type='text' and the formControlName directive set to 'name'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: binding a form control to an input
<input type="text" formControlName="username">
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain an input field bound to the 'name' form control.
successCriteria: The template includes an <input> element with formControlName='name'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input field, but make sure it uses formControlName='name' for binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field is missing or not properly bound. Add <input type='text' formControlName='name'> to the template.

steps.title: Add email input field with form control binding
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add an email input field with formControlName binding for the 'email' control.
steps.hint: Use the same pattern as the name input field, but with type='email' and formControlName='email'.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Similar: another form control binding -->
<input type="email" formControlName="email" placeholder="Enter your email" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will have both name and email input fields bound to their respective form controls.
successCriteria: An email input field with formControlName='email' is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input field, but check that it has type='email' and formControlName='email'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The email input field is missing or incorrectly configured. Review the form control binding syntax.

steps.title: Add submit button wired to form submission
steps.instruction: Add a submit button inside the form that triggers the form submission when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the <button> element with type='submit' inside the form. The button should be placed after the email input field.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Submit button in an Angular form
<button type="submit">Submit Form</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a submit button that triggers the onSubmit method when clicked.
successCriteria: A submit button element is added inside the form, after the email input field.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it's inside the form and has type='submit'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The submit button is missing or not properly placed inside the form.

steps.title: Display validation error messages
steps.instruction: Add error message displays below each input field that show when the form control is invalid and touched.
steps.hint: Use Angular's form control properties like 'invalid' and 'touched' with *ngIf to conditionally show error messages.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: conditional error display
This field is required
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will display validation error messages when users interact with invalid fields.
successCriteria: Error messages appear below each input when the field is invalid and has been touched.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some error messages, but make sure both name and email fields have them and they appear conditionally.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error messages are missing or don't appear correctly. Check that you're using *ngIf with the form control's invalid and touched properties.
